## Purpose and deployment shape
eqMac v1.3.2 is a macOS system-audio processor: capture system audio through a virtual CoreAudio driver, apply volume/EQ effects in a native app, and route processed audio to selected hardware outputs. The shipped UI is an Angular/TypeScript bundle embedded by the macOS app and designed for remotely hosted, OTA-updatable use. Primary native entry points are `native/app/Source/AppDelegate.swift`, `native/app/Source/Application.swift`, and `native/driver/Source/EQMDriver.swift`.

## Native application orchestration
The Swift/AppKit application owns lifecycle, native window/status-item management, audio-engine setup, settings, and the bridge to the web UI. `Application` coordinates feature subsystems; `ApplicationState` and specialized state/data-bus pairs model application-facing state and notifications. Relevant paths: `native/app/Source/Application.swift`, `native/app/Source/ApplicationDataBus.swift`, `native/app/Source/UI/Bridge.swift`.

## System-audio capture driver
A separate user-space CoreAudio Audio Server Plug-in implements eqMac’s virtual loopback/passthrough device. It exposes device, stream, client, and control objects and supplies audio to the app through the driver/app boundary described as a secure memory tunnel. The driver is its own Xcode project and deployable system component, not part of the Angular runtime. Paths: `native/driver/Source/EQMPlugIn.swift`, `native/driver/Source/EQMDevice.swift`, `native/driver/Source/EQMStream.swift`.

## Audio pipeline and routing
`Engine` is the application’s audio-processing coordinator. Sources represent system capture and input sources; effects are applied to the stream; outputs route resulting audio to physical targets. Device-event handling responds to CoreAudio topology changes. The principal control/data path is: driver/system source → engine → enabled effects/volume → selected output device. Paths: `native/app/Source/Audio/Engine.swift`, `native/app/Source/Audio/Sources/System/SystemSource.swift`, `native/app/Source/Audio/Outputs/Outputs.swift`.

## Effects and volume domain
Effects are organized behind common effect abstractions, with basic and advanced equalizer implementations plus persistent state and event buses. Volume separately handles boost/balance-style state; the UI mirrors these domains. This boundary isolates DSP/control logic from presentation and transport. Paths: `native/app/Source/Audio/Effects/Effect.swift`, `native/app/Source/Audio/Effects/Equalizers/Equalizers.swift`, `native/app/Source/Audio/Volume/Volume.swift`.

## UI hosting and native bridge
The native app hosts an embedded web UI (`native/app/Assets/Embedded/ui.zip`) and exposes native capabilities through `Bridge.swift`. Angular bootstraps from `ui/src/main.ts` into `AppModule`; bridge/data services provide the client-side boundary for reading state and issuing native actions. UI sections map directly to audio domains—source, outputs, effects, volume, and settings. Paths: `ui/src/main.ts`, `ui/src/app/services/bridge.service.ts`, `ui/src/app/app.module.ts`.

## Angular feature composition
The Angular UI is a desktop-control surface rather than an independent backend. Section services/components manage UI interactions for equalizers, output selection, sources, and volume, while reusable controls live in a shared component module. Paths: `ui/src/app/sections/effects/equalizers/equalizers.service.ts`, `ui/src/app/sections/outputs/outputs.service.ts`, `modules/components/src/components.module.ts`.

## Runtime dependencies and boundaries
Material runtimes are macOS/AppKit, CoreAudio/AVAudioEngine, Swift, and an Angular/TypeScript web runtime. Native persistence/filesystem, networking, scripts, and window APIs remain behind the app bridge; the driver is a privileged system-audio integration boundary. Shared Swift primitives support native app/driver implementations. Paths: `native/shared/Package.swift`, `native/app/Source/Networking/Networking.swift`, `native/app/Source/Settings/Settings.swift`.
